question: Ram covers 500 km distance in 20 hours in traffic; he covered some distance by bike at 30 km/h, and rest by car at 20 km/h. The distance covered by bike (in km) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed for the entire journey = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 500 ÷ 20 = 25 km/h.

Using alligation on speeds (Bike: 30 km/h, Car: 20 km/h, Average: 25 km/h):

Ratio of time taken = (25 − 20) : (30 − 25) = 5 : 5 = 1 : 1.

Time spent on the bike = 1/2 of 20 hours = 10 hours.

Distance covered by bike = Speed × Time = 30 × 10 = 300 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 300 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 500 km

Total time = 20 hours

Speed of bike = 30 km/h

Speed of car = 20 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd1114e5717ad7e8eae7c3538a815d797ccec15a6b0588161cd26ede8fe8cc1d.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the time traveled by bike be t hours.

⇒ Then, time traveled by car = (20 − t) hours.

⇒ Total Distance = Distance by bike + Distance by car

⇒ 30t + 20(20 − t) = 500

⇒ 30t + 400 − 20t = 500

⇒ 10t = 100

⇒ t = 10 hours

⇒ Distance covered by bike = Speed × Time = 30 × 10 = 300 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 300 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

It is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Overall Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Alligation in Speed and Distance

When applying the alligation cross-method on speeds, the resulting ratio strictly represents the ratio of the **time** taken at those speeds, not the ratio of distances covered.

Relative Speed

For bodies moving in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds (v₁ + v₂). For bodies moving in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (|v₁ − v₂|).
